units: <cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Job 39:25">Targ. Job XXXIX, 25</cite>; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Sotah 49a:10">Sot. 49ᵃ</cite> <he>מוֹרְחִינָא ריחא וכ׳</he> I smell &c., v. <cite ref="D00160"><he>דַּהֲנוּנִיתָא</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Bava Batra 73b:10">B. Bath. 73ᵇ</cite> <he>ומוֹרַח ביה</he>, v. <cite ref="P01078"><he>עַפְרָא</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Sanhedrin 93b:8">Snh. 93ᵇ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Isaiah 11:3">Is. XI, 3</cite>, sq.) <he>במשיח כתיב דמורח ודאין</he> of the Messiah it is written that he smells (of a man) and judges (of his guilt or innocence); <he>ניחזי אנן אי מרח ודאין</he> let us see whether he (Bar Koziba) smells &c.; <he>כיון דחזיוהו דלא מריח וכ׳</he> when they saw that he could not judge by the scent, they killed him; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 284">Yalk. Is. 284</cite>.
<cite ref="Berakhot 43b:4">Ber. 43ᵇ</cite> <he>האי מאן דמורח באתרוגא וכ׳</he> he that smells an Ethrog …, must say the benediction &c.
<cite ref="Yoma 82b:2">Yoma 82ᵇ</cite> <he>ההיא עוברא דאָרְחָא</he> a woman with child that smelled, v. <cite ref="T00615">preced.</cite>
<cite ref="Shabbat 110a:4">Sabb. 110ᵃ</cite> <he>דמורח ריחא וכ׳</he> (not <he>דמירח</he>) when it (the snake) smells it &c.; a. e.
